'''George Larenzo Gilder III'''<ref>{{cite web |title=George Larenzo Gilder III () - Basketball Stats, Height, Age |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/players/178029-george-larenzo-gilder-iii |website=FIBA Basketball |access-date=9 July 2026}}</ref> (born January 24, 1985) is an American professional [[basketball]] player. He played college basketball for [[McNeese State Cowboys basketball|McNeese State]], [[Tyler Junior College]] and [[Northwestern State Demons basketball|Northwestern State]].

==High school career==
Gilder attended [[DeSoto High School (DeSoto, Texas)|DeSoto High School]] in [[DeSoto, Texas]], where he was a member of the 2003 Texas 5A State Championship winning team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/recruiting/player-Trey-Gilder-51537 |title=Trey Gilder – Yahoo! Sports |work=Yahoo.com |accessdate=October 8, 2013}}</ref>

==College career==
In 2003–04, Gilder played briefly for [[McNeese State University]] before playing for [[Tyler Junior College]] from 2004 to 2006.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ridiculousupside.com/2009/4/29/858845/summer-league-profiles-trey-gilder |title=D-League Profiles: Trey Gilder |work=RidiculousUpside.com |publisher=SB Nation |date=April 29, 2009 |accessdate=October 8, 2013}}</ref>

Gilder played two years at [[Northwestern State Demons men's basketball|Northwestern State University]] from 2006 to 2008. He averaged 14.1 points, 4.7 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 1.2 steals per game over his Northwestern State college career.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/trey-gilder-1.html |title=Trey Gilder Stats |work=Sports-Reference.com  |accessdate=January 28, 2015}}</ref> Gilder was named to the 2006–07 Southland Conference All-Tournament Team in his first year with the Demons. He went on to be named to the 2007–08 first-team All-[[Southland Conference]] after leading the Demons in points (16.4) and rebounds (6.2) as a senior, finishing ninth in school history in points in a single season (542).<ref name=claws>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/maine/gilder20091130.html RED CLAWS ACQUIRE TREY GILDER] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110817132506/http://www.nba.com/dleague/maine/gilder20091130.html |date=August 17, 2011 }}</ref>

==Professional career==

===2008–09 season===
After going undrafted in the [[2008 NBA draft]], Gilder was selected by the [[Colorado 14ers]] in the second round of the [[2008 NBA Development League Draft]] on November 7, 2008. He went on to help the 14ers win the 2009 NBA D-League championship as he averaged 13.6 points in 54 games on the season.<ref>[https://www.basketball-reference.com/nbdl/players/g/gildetr01d.html Trey Gilder D-League Stats]</ref>

===2009–10 season===
In July 2009, Gilder joined the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] for the 2009 [[NBA Summer League]] and later signed with the team on August 27, 2009.<ref>[http://www.grizzlybearblues.com/2009/8/27/1005287/the-skinny-grizzlies-sign-trey The Skinny: Grizzlies Sign Trey Gilder]</ref> However, he was waived by the Grizzlies on November 5 after appearing in six preseason games and two regular season games.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies_waive_gilder-0901105.html Grizzlies waive Trey Gilder]</ref> On November 30, he was acquired by the [[Maine Red Claws]].<ref name="claws" /> On March 5, 2010, he was traded to the [[New Mexico Thunderbirds|Albuquerque Thunderbirds]] in exchange for Kurt Looby.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/maine/looby_030510.html RED CLAWS ACQUIRE KURT LOOBY AT TRADE DEADLINE]</ref>

===2010–11 season===
In July 2010, Gilder joined the [[Orlando Magic]] for the Orlando Summer League and the [[Atlanta Hawks]] for the Las Vegas Summer League. In November 2010, he signed with [[KK Zagreb]] of the Croatian [[A-1 Liga]]<ref>[http://www.tportal.hr/sport/kosarka/95558/Zagreb-doveo-Rancica-i-novog-Amerikanca.html Zagreb doveo Rančića i novog Amerikanca] {{in lang|hr}}</ref> but lasted just two games for parting ways with the club. On December 7, 2010, he signed with the [[Sydney Kings]] for the rest of the [[2010–11 NBL season]].<ref>[https://au.news.yahoo.com/thewest/sport/a/8465693/kings-sign-former-memphis-grizzly/ Kings sign former Memphis Grizzly]</ref><ref>[http://wwos.ninemsn.com.au/article.aspx?id=8178114 Kings sign former NBA player]</ref> In 20 games for the Kings, he averaged 13.2 points, 5.5 rebounds and 2.2 assists per game.<ref>[http://www.foxsportspulse.com/team_info.cgi?action=PSTATS&pID=192050478&client=0-189-88249-119318-369912 Player statistics for Trey Gilder]</ref>

===2011–12 season===
On December 12, 2011, Gilder signed with the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz_signs_tinsley_mcleod_glider.html Jazz Signs Jamaal Tinsley, Keith McLeod and Trey Gilder]</ref> However, he was later waived by the Jazz on December 21, 2011.<ref>[http://www.ksl.com/?sid=18588828 Utah Jazz waive four players]</ref> Having held the returning players rights of Gilder following the name change from the New Mexico Thunderbirds, the [[Canton Charge]] traded his rights to the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] on January 3, 2012.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/canton/news/charge_acquire_pick_from_skyfo_2012_01_03.html Charge Acquire Pick from Skyforce]</ref>

===2012 off-season===
On April 18, 2012, Gilder signed with [[Trotamundos de Carabobo]] of Venezuela for the rest of the 2012 [[Liga Profesional de Baloncesto|LPB]] season.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/91427/trotamundos-de-carabobo-tab-trey-gilder.html Trotamundos de Carabobo tab Trey Gilder]</ref> In July 2012, he joined the [[Miami Heat]] for the 2012 NBA Summer League, and the following month, he signed with [[Cañeros del Este]] of the [[Liga Nacional de Baloncesto]].<ref>[http://www.melvynlopez.com/2012/08/ex-nba-trey-gilder-llega-este-miercoles.html EX NBA TREY GILDER LLEGA ESTE MIERCOLES PARA LOS CAÑEROS DEL ESTE] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304091437/http://www.melvynlopez.com/2012/08/ex-nba-trey-gilder-llega-este-miercoles.html |date=March 4, 2016 }} {{in lang|es}}</ref>

===2012–13 season===
On September 26, 2012, Gilder signed with the Utah Jazz, returning to the franchise for a second stint.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-signs-four-free-agents Jazz Signs Four Free Agents]</ref> However, he was waived again on October 18, 2012, after appearing in two preseason games.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-waives-two-players Jazz Waives Two Players]</ref> In February 2013, he returned to Trotamundos de Carabobo but left the team after two months.

===2013–14 season===
On February 21, 2014, Gilder signed with [[Halcones de Xalapa]] of Mexico for the rest of the 2013–14 ([[Liga Nacional de Baloncesto Profesional|LNBP]] season.<ref>[http://www.court-side.com/news/blog/trey-gilder-joins-halcones-xalapa-2/ Trey Gilder joins Halcones Xalapa]</ref> He later returned to Trotamundos in May for a third stint.

===2014–15 season===
On January 28, 2015, Gilder was acquired by the [[Austin Spurs]].<ref>[http://austin.dleague.nba.com/news/austin-spurs-acquire-trey-gilder/ AUSTIN SPURS ACQUIRE TREY GILDER]</ref> On February 17, he was traded to the [[Westchester Knicks]] in exchange for the returning player rights of [[Richard Howell (basketball)|Richard Howell]].<ref>[http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=4928089 Sherrod Wright Returns to Westchester]</ref>

Shot the 3 that clinched the championship in the Dominican Republic in 2018.

MVP of the year 2018 Venezuela.

===2015–16 season===
On December 20, 2015, Gilder signed with [[Panteras de Miranda]] of the [[Liga Profesional de Baloncesto|Venezuelan League]].<ref>[http://www.latinbasket.com/Venezuela/news/431996/Panteras-land-Trey-Gilder Panteras land Trey Gilder]</ref>

===2017–18 season===
In March 2018, Gilder signed with Rafael Barias of the Dominican Torneo de Baloncesto Superior (TBS), making his debut on March 21 in an 80–78 win over Huellas del Siglo.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.eurobasket.com/boxScores/Dominican%20Republic/2018/0321_9630_21365.asp|title=Regular Season Round 1: Rafael Barias - Huellas Del Siglo 80-78|work=Eurobasket.com|date=March 21, 2018|accessdate=May 5, 2018}}</ref> After the season ended, he re-signed with Panteras de Miranda.<ref>{{cite web|first=Francisco|last=Vega|url=http://www.latinbasket.com/Venezuela/news/532419/Panteras-welcome-back-Gilder,-ex-Rafael-Barias|title=Panteras welcome back Gilder, ex Rafael Barias|work=LatinBasket.com|date=May 14, 2018|accessdate=May 15, 2018}}</ref>

===2019–20 season===
On August 17, 2019, Gilder signed with the [[Saga Ballooners]] of the [[B.League]].<ref>{{cite web |title=新加入選手のお知らせ |url=https://ballooners.jp/news/detail/id=44161 |website=佐賀バルーナーズ |access-date=December 29, 2024 |date=August 17, 2019}}</ref>

==Personal==
Gilder is the son of Judith Redwine, and he has a brother, Keri.<ref>Glider graduated from DeSoto High School in 2003, DeSoto, TX, obtained his Associates Degree from Tyler Jr. College in Tyler, TX and his Bachelors Degree from Northwestern State in Louisiana. [http://www.nsudemons.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=924 Trey Gilder - 2007 Men's Basketball]</ref>
